n: A prophecy about Moab, Israel’s neighbor east of the Dead Sea, descended from Abraham’s nephew Lot. Its major cities, Ar and Kir, are destroyed overnight and fall silent.

f.g: A main city near the Arnon River (Numbers 21:28).
Probably Kir-hareseth, Moab’s fortified capital (modern Kerak).

n: Moabites go up to their temples and high places at Dibon to weep, and wail over Nebo and Medeba. Shaved heads and cut beards were signs of deep mourning.

f.g: “The house” — likely a temple of Chemosh, Moab’s god.
A Moabite city where the famous Mesha Stele was found.
A town near the mountain where Moses viewed the promised land (Deuteronomy 34:1).

n: People wear sackcloth in the streets and wail on their flat rooftops, weeping uncontrollably.

f.g: Rough goat-hair cloth worn in mourning.
Flat roofs, used as living and worship spaces.

n: Cries from Heshbon and Elealeh are heard as far as Jahaz. Even Moab’s soldiers cry out, their spirits broken.

f.g: A city north of Moab, once the Amorite capital (Numbers 21:26).

f.w: his life shall be grievous unto him

n: Isaiah himself grieves for Moab, showing God’s compassion even for Israel’s enemies. Refugees flee south toward Zoar, weeping up the slope of Luhith and crying along the road to Horonaim.

f.w: My heart shall cry out for Moab

f.g: A town at the south end of the Dead Sea (Genesis 19:22).

f.w: an heifer of three years old

n: The springs of Nimrim have dried up; grass withers and nothing green remains. Even the land mourns.

f.g: A stream or oasis in southern Moab.

n: Fleeing families carry whatever wealth they can across the Brook of the Willows, Moab’s southern border.

f.g: Probably the Zered valley, Moab’s border with Edom.

n: The wailing spreads to every border of Moab, reaching Eglaim and Beer-elim.
The waters of Dimon run red with blood, and even more trouble is coming — lions will attack those who escape. “Dimon” sounds like the Hebrew word for blood (dam).

f.g: Likely Dibon, spelled to make a wordplay with dam, “blood.”
